title: session_status surfaces SQLite "database is locked" as untyped storage_error instead of the typed retryable control_store_busy
outcome: session_status surfaces SQLite "database is locked" as untyped storage_error instead of the typed retryable control_store_busy
acceptance: A control session_status call that meets SQLITE_BUSY or SQLITE_LOCKED (after any configured busy wait) returns the typed retryable refusal the host protocol already defines for store contention (control_store_busy), not storage_error with "SQLite operation failed: database is locked". Proved by a deterministic test that holds a conflicting writer lock while session_status runs.

Every other control operation that can hit the same lock path (session_bind, turn_evaluate, begin, checkpoint, end) classifies busy or locked the same way, shown by a test per operation or a shared classification test that covers them all.

Genuine storage failures (corruption, I/O, a failed rollback or COMMIT) still return storage_error. The fix doesn't hide real errors as busy, and doesn't widen any retry allowlist beyond store contention.

completion.summary: Landed typed retryable session_status contention handling with deterministic writer-lock regressions, preserved genuine storage failures, and updated keyless retry contract. Full gate and both reviews passed; fresh independent closure evaluation passed all three criteria.
